summary.text: Previously healthy 4-year and 5-month-old girl presented on 26 May 2025 with an 8-day history of fever and cough and a truncal rash that began one day before admission; examination showed ill appearance, pharyngeal injection and an erythematous truncal rash, with CRP 80.54 mg/L and chest radiography consolidation. She received amoxicillin earlier at local clinics.

Presumptive pneumonia and acute urticaria were diagnosed; she was admitted and given intravenous ceftriaxone, azithromycin and supportive care including cetirizine, IV diphenhydramine and IV hydration. By hospital day 3 CRP was 28.47 mg/L and Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM was positive; total IgE was 1357 KU/L.

A new extensive urticarial rash developed on the face, hands and thighs despite improving fever and cough; intravenous hydrocortisone (300 mg every day for 5 days) did not help, so a single subcutaneous dose of omalizumab 150 mg was given on the eighth hospital day.

The rash resolved the next day and she was discharged home; a minor recurrence a week later resolved with oral antihistamines, and she remained symptom-free without severe complications over 6 months of follow-up.

summary.text: A 1-year and 8-month-old girl developed diffuse erythematous itching plaques after her third Enterovirus vaccination with cough, rhinorrhea and vomiting on 13 June 2025; she had no prior history of allergies or adverse reactions to previous vaccinations. Leukocytosis (WBC 12.9), CRP 12.7 mg/L and an elevated Mycoplasma IgM (1240.6 U/mL) were found, with total IgE 32.6 KU/L within the normal range.
Initial antihistamines, intravenous hydrocortisone and azithromycin were ineffective; four days after symptom onset, for worsening urticaria, omalizumab 150 mg was given off-label.

The rash markedly improved within 48 h and she was discharged in stable condition; short-term follow-up showed complete resolution, only minor recurrences resolved with oral antihistamines over three months, no serious long-term side effects, and no further episodes at telephone follow-up in November 2025.
